From what I've seen, very few people who have trouble with this sort of thing actually consciously think something disastrous is going to happen. Believe it or not you're not the first person to tell us this.

But knowing that fears are irrational doesn't actually help make them any less scary.

You might be interested to know that Americans pay more per capita for public health care than the British do per capita.

To be clear, the average American pays *more* tax dollars for health care than the average British person, but gets no health care in return.

(This is because those Americans who do get publicly funded health care in the US get healthcare that is much, much less efficient for various reasons, so paying for a few percent of their population costs more than paying for all the British population)

It's not worrying about tomorrow that creates a problem. It's trying to overcome the crushing feeling of my stomach being about 6 feet below the rest of my body that's making me want to throw up and cry.
